definitions.gloss: running into someone; bumping into; unexpected encounter
definitions.explanation: An unplanned meeting with someone, often in an awkward or unwelcome situation. Literally refers to two heads bumping together.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}で{元|もと}カノと{鉢合|はちあ}わせした。
examples.english: I ran into my ex-girlfriend at the station.

examples.japanese: {廊下|ろうか}で{上司|じょうし}と{鉢合|はちあ}わせして{気|き}まずかった。
examples.english: I bumped into my boss in the hallway and it was awkward.

examples.japanese: {泥棒|どろぼう}は{逃|に}げようとしたところ、{帰宅|きたく}した{住人|じゅうにん}と{鉢合|はちあ}わせしてしまった。
examples.english: The burglar tried to escape but ran right into the returning resident.

notes:
An unexpected, often unwelcome encounter. The word comes from the image of two people bumping heads ({鉢|はち} refers to the top of the head).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鉢合|はちあ}わせする (to run into someone)
- {鉢合|はちあ}わせになる (to end up running into each other)
- {偶然|ぐうぜん}{鉢合|はちあ}わせする (to accidentally run into)

Often implies the encounter is inconvenient, embarrassing, or unwanted. Used more dramatically than {出|で}くわす (to come across) or {偶然|ぐうぜん}{会|あ}う (to meet by chance).
